Note::html_escape¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::html_escape() const

Escape The Five Markup-Significant Characters¶

html_escape() rewrites each cell so it can be dropped into HTML or XML text without being parsed as markup. It replaces exactly five characters with their entity references:

Character

Replacement

&

&amp;

<

&lt;

>

&gt;

"

&quot;

'

&#39;

Escaping " and ' as well as the three structural characters means the result is also safe inside a single- or double-quoted attribute value, not only in element content.

Every other byte is copied through untouched — letters, digits, whitespace, and all non-ASCII UTF-8 (café — € is unchanged). The operation works on UTF-8 text and on bytes-mode Notes alike, preserves shape, keeps the input’s encoding tag, and returns a fresh Note.

html_escape() is not idempotent: applying it twice escapes the & in the entities it produced (<a> → &lt;a&gt; → &amp;lt;a&amp;gt;), so escape exactly once, at the point of output. The inverse is html_unescape.

Example 1: The Five Characters, In 1-D¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"a & b < c > d \" e ' f", "plain"}).html_escape())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["a &amp; b &lt; c &gt; d &quot; e &#39; f", "plain"]

A cell with none of the five characters ("plain") is returned as-is.

Example 2: Non-ASCII Is Left Alone¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"café — €"}).html_escape() << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["café — €"]

Example 3: Shape Is Preserved¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({{"<x>", "y&z"}}).html_escape())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1, 2], dim=2, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["&lt;x&gt;", "y&amp;z"]
]

Example 4: Escaping Twice Double-Escapes¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"<a>"}).html_escape().html_escape() << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["&amp;lt;a&amp;gt;"]

See Also¶

  • Note::html_unescape: the inverse.

  • Note::json_escape: escaping for JSON string bodies instead of markup.

  • NoteTexAccessor::escape: escaping TeX special characters.
